new_statements.quote: 3. Акцентология и тонология. Ударение в зиало динамического типа, фиксированное, преимущественно падает на последний слог корня. Ударение не искажается ни тоном, ни долготой гласных: безударные гласные могут быть долгими или краткими, и влияние тона на ударение никак не отмечено. Следствием окситонального ударения, по-видимому, является редукция гласных в начальных слогах многосложных лексем, о которой говорилось выше. Тон в зиало является фонологической (смыслоразличительной) категорией и играет важнейшую роль в системе морфосинтаксиса.
new_statements.translation: 3. Accentology and tonology. Stress in Zialo is of the dynamic type, fixed, and falls predominantly on the last syllable of the root. Stress is not distorted either by tone or by vowel length: unstressed vowels may be long or short, and no influence of tone on stress has been noted. A consequence of the oxytonic stress is apparently the reduction of vowels in the initial syllables of polysyllabic lexemes, which was discussed above. Tone in Zialo is a phonological (meaning-distinguishing) category and plays a most important role in the morphosyntactic system.
new_statements.citation: Бабаев, К. В. 2011. Фонологический и морфосинтаксический профиль языка зиало. Вопросы филологии 2011, № 3 (39): 37–51. (Glottolog id 313186 cites the title as 'Fonologičeskij i morfologičeskij profil' yazyka Zialo'; the printed title reads 'морфосинтаксический'.)
new_statements.locator: p. 41, §3 'Акцентология и тонология' (PDF page 5 of the 15-page offprint); the vowel-reduction rule it refers back to is on p. 39–40 (§2: reduction of high and mid-high vowels only in initial syllables before l, rarely w, y: pélé [pele] 'road', gèwɔ̀lày [gəwɔlay] 'something big').
new_statements.reading: tone language with a stress statement
new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Opened (15-page A4 offprint, text layer, InDesign 2012; running head "Бабаев К.В. PDF page 5 = printed p. 41, left column, heading "3. Акцентология и тонология": the quoted passage is there word for word (line-break hyphenation joined): "Ударение в зиало динамического типа, фиксированное, преимущественно падает на последний слог корня. Ударение не искажается ни тоном, ни долготой гласных: безударные гласные могут быть долгими или краткими, и влияние тона на ударение никак не отмечено. Следствием окситонального…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Zialo is a two-level tone language (H, L; tone-bearing unit = vowel, tonal domain = the metrical foot, usually a disyllabic word) that also has dynamic, fixed stress: stress falls on the last syllable of the root (oxytonic). Stress is independent of tone and of vowel length; unstressed initial-syllable vowels of polysyllables reduce.
new_statements.exceptions: None listed; the author hedges with 'преимущественно' (predominantly) on the last syllable of the root.
new_statements.domain_note: Domain is the root ('последний слог корня'), not the phonological word: suffixes/clitics such as the definite marker -y and tonal clitics are outside the stated domain. The article also states that the basic prosodic unit is the metrical foot, generally corresponding to the word and typically two syllables. No statement on citation forms vs phrase-level prominence.
new_statements.identity_note: The source describes Zialo as a whole (zial1235; ISO zil), based on Babaev's 2010 fieldwork; it notes five dialects with Lawolozu the most distinctive but does not restrict the stress statement to one dialect. Glottolog lists the 2011 article title as 'Fonologičeskij i morfologičeskij profil'', while the printed title is 'Фонологический и морфосинтаксический профиль языка зиало' (Вопросы филологии 2011 № 3 (39): 37–51).

sources.note: §3 'Акцентология и тонология', p. 41: dynamic, fixed stress predominantly on the last syllable of the root; independent of tone and vowel length; oxytonic stress drives initial-syllable vowel reduction; two level tones H/L plus a super-high on one conjunction; tone domain = metrical foot. Retrieved as the author's offprint from the Wayback Machine copy of his site (http://web.archive.org/web/2014id_/http://babaev.net/).

sources.citation: 'Зиало' page of the former portal Языки манде (Kunstkamera), archived 2019-05-27.
sources.note: Short note: 25,000 speakers, five dialects (Lawolozu most distinctive), grammar and tonal system close to Loma, lexicon closer to Bandi/Mende; no stress statement, no PDFs. The live mandelang.kunstkamera.ru domain now serves an unrelated site.

sources.citation: Wilhoit, Laura. 2011. Book review: Babaev, Kirill. Zialo: the Newly-Discovered Mande Language of Guinea. München: Lincom Europa, 2010. Mandenkan 47: 97–102. doi:10.4000/15z7j
sources.note: Summarises the Lincom grammar's phonology chapter (syllable types V, CV, Vy, CVy; tone rules Rightward Spreading, Suprasegmental Morpheme Influence, Clitic Tone Variability, Syntagmic Border Limit; tone classes in the vocabulary). No mention of stress or accent. OpenEdition sits behind the Anubis JS filter, so curl could not save the page/PDF; read via web lookups at https://journals.openedition.org/mandenkan/4457.

sources.citation: Babaev, Kirill. 2010. Person marking in South-West Mande languages: a tentative reconstruction. Mandenkan 46: 3–48. doi:10.4000/163hk
sources.note: Comparative person-marking study with Zialo data; discusses lexical tone of markers only, nothing on stress (web lookups of https://journals.openedition.org/mandenkan/4603).
Only that tonology resembles Loma and that nasal vowels and initial consonant alternations are prominent; no stress information; external links point to the dead mandelang portal and the Lincom shop.
